steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Photography's history: from daguerreotypes to digital, each technical advance changed what and how photographers could communicate.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key movements: pictorialism (soft, painterly), straight photography (sharp, unmanipulated), modernism (formal experimentation), postmodernism (conceptual, appropriated).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Photography has enormous social and cultural impact — it shapes how we see the world, from photojournalism to advertising to social media.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Understanding why and how photographers work helps you make more informed, intentional choices in your own practice.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring photographers and photography history. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with photographers and photography history. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with photographers and photography history. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to photographers and photography history, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to re | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
